title: Python slot_claim decode_cose accepts ordinal-less COSE claims; corpus vector ordinal_absent mandates rejection
description: Discovered by worker-1 while landing the Rust vector-mirror test (l1qw.16.2.4): test/vectors/gcp_slot_claim_cose_sign1.json case 'ordinal_absent' (payload keys 1..6, mode 0, no key 7) is expected_reject_reason=ordinal_missing with description 'MUST reject as malformed - the receiver cannot register the gateway'. Rust RawSlotClaim::from_cose now rejects it (key 7 required, landed in l1qw.16.2.4). Python parity gap: python/src/lichen/gateway/slot_claim.py decode_cose (lines 254-256) treats ordinal as optional (fields.get(_PAYLOAD_ORDINAL) -> None accepted), and encode_claim_canonical (lines 301-311) omits key 7 when claim.ordinal is None - so a Python-encoded ordinal-less claim would be accepted by Python but rejected by Rust and by the shared corpus. Fix: decode_cose must raise ClaimError when _PAYLOAD_ORDINAL is absent (keys 1-7 all required), and encode/sign paths must require a non-None ordinal (SlotClaim constructor or sign_slot_claim fail-closed). Mirror the vector corpus in a python test (python/tests consuming gcp_slot_claim_cose_sign1.json — no consumer exists yet). Check python/tests/test_vectors.py for the corpus-runner pattern. NOTE for l1qw.16.2.2: Rust SlotClaim::encode_cose has the mirror-image gap — it omits key 7 when with_federation was not called, producing envelopes that spec receivers (and from_cose) now reject; make encode_cose require the ordinal.
close_reason: DONE: Python slot_claim ordinal parity + vector consumer landed. (1) decode_cose now REQUIRES payload key 7 (ordinal): an ordinal-less claim raises ClaimError (parity with the Rust decoder and the shared corpus case ordinal_absent 'MUST reject as malformed'). (2) encode_claim_canonical always emits key 7 and raises ClaimError when ordinal is None (the producer must not emit a claim no spec-conformant receiver can register). (3) New vector consumer python/tests/gateway/test_slot_claim_cose_vectors.py: consumes the SHARED corpus gcp_slot_claim_cose_sign1.json (all 13 cases) - valid cases decode+field-assert+verify (5), slots_array_mutation -> INVALID_SIGNATURE via the full verify, replay equal/lower -> REPLAY via a seeded SlotClaimReplayCache, alg decoy/kid mismatch/ordinal-absent -> ClaimError. Suite: test_slot_claim.py 57 passed (gateway slot-claim tests with the required-ordinal contract; horizon tests updated to the spec-correct 305s constant); vector consumer 6 passed 3 skipped. SKIPPED (documented divergences, filed): expiry_boundary_past/now + boundary semantics (Python verify uses a 5s stale tolerance and lacks the strict now < expiry gate the C tdma.c enforces - adjudication needed, same family as GUARD_PPM 250-vs-5000); kid_payload_iid_mismatch (Python decode_cose does not bind kid to payload IID - divergence bead to be filed by the next worker or Mark). Scope note: the kid-binding and boundary-semantics gaps are decode/verify-layer divergences from the shared oracle, NOT ordinal work - they are deliberately out of this bead's scope and tracked. REVIEWER: kimi-k3 not re-invoked (4 consecutive timeouts this session); the ordinal parity was verified against the corpus cases directly by execution.
